- Overestimate prices when sentiment is high (especially >0.5) and recent prices are trending up — model tends to overshoot.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low (especially <0.3) or shows negative momentum — model fails to recognize downward pressure.
- Avoid sharp upward spikes in forecast when sentiment is weak or recent prices are consolidating — model often overreacts.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is significantly above recent 10-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment strongly supports.
- Lagged correction: if true outcome is below forecast by >5% for 2+ consecutive days, adjust next forecast downward by 2–5%.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are prone to overconfidence in early days — reduce first 5–7 days’ forecast by 3–5% if sentiment is neutral or declining.
- Sentiment-driven bias: if sentiment drops below 0.2 after a spike, model often fails to correct — apply downward bias of 2–4% for next 3–5 days.
